data.title: Trump bought up to $323k of Nvidia stock in September, disclosure shows
data.description:
WASHINGTON — US President Donald Trump bought as much as US$265,000 (S$323,000) in Nvidia stock and sold as much as US$15,000 worth of the stock ​in September, weeks before reports surfaced of CEO Jensen Huang's ties to an alleged Chinese spy, according to Trump's latest financial disclosure released on Thursday (Nov 19).

US lawmakers have been asking questions about Trump's knowledge of Huang's personal life, and the president has said he "was amazed" by the allegations against Huang, who is among the president's closest allies in Silicon Valley.

Trump administration officials are currently weighing policies ⁠that could shape Nvidia's future, including rules governing exports of ​its advanced chips. Nvidia faces heightened scrutiny after news reports surfaced that Huang had a romantic relationship with a woman accused of spying for Beijing. Reuters has not independently confirmed that the woman is a spy.

The Nvidia ⁠trades were among hundreds the president made in September, according to the disclosure signed ​by Trump on November 1 and made ​public by the US Office of Government Ethics ⁠on Thursday. In August, Trump bought as much as US$1.6 million worth of Nvidia shares and sold as much as US$1 million worth, Reuters previously reported.

Trump also bought as much as US$315,000 in SpaceX stock in September, according to the same disclosure. SpaceX is a US ​military contractor run by Trump's former adviser Elon Musk. 

The company has billions of dollars' worth of contracts with the US government, and its fortunes are often tied to approvals from federal agencies. Trump has traded SpaceX stock over the course of his second term as president, including in June and July 2026.

Reuters could not immediately determine the precise amount of Trump's trades because federal officials use ranges to declare the value of their assets on their financial disclosure forms.

Trump's portfolio managed separately: White House

White House spokesperson Davis Ingle said in a statement that third-party financial institutions independently manage the president's portfolio and replicate "recognised indexes, such as the Schwab 1000".

"Neither President Trump nor any member of his family has any ability to direct, influence or provide input regarding how the portfolio is invested or when investments are bought or sold," Ingle said.

Nvidia is the world's leading maker of advanced AI chips, widely used to develop cutting-edge AI systems. The US has for years sought to limit China's access to Nvidia's most advanced chips, driven by concerns that China could use them to build weapons or superior AI tools.

Nvidia executives, including Huang, have argued for broader access to China. Chinese companies and researchers have also repeatedly found ways around the US export restrictions.

On Monday, the Trump administration said it would further limit China's access to advanced AI chips from companies such as ​Nvidia by restricting shipments of advanced chips to Southeast Asian countries, which Chinese companies have used to access computing power to train AI models.

The New York Times reported that Trump had been briefed in 2025 on Huang's relationship with the woman and on intelligence that she was giving information to the Chinese government, ​and that he chose not to act on ​the findings. Questioned about the New York Times reporting, Trump said he "was amazed" by the allegations against Huang.

data.title: Esso drops fuel prices for first time since Sept 14
data.description:
Chandra Asri-owned Esso has become the latest major fuel company here to drop fuel prices.

In a price board update posted on Thursday (Nov 19) evening, Esso announced that it has reduced prices across its 92-, 95- and 98-octane petrol grades, as well as diesel.

The 3-cent per litre reduction mirrored the same drop posted by Caltex on Nov 4, and Shell and Sinopec on Nov 18.

SPC is the only major fuel company here that has not adjusted prices this week.

However, the PetroChina-owned company was also the only retailer that did not join in the last round of price hikes recorded between Oct 29 and Nov 2.

Instead, SPC's last posted price adjustments were on Oct 16.

Following the latest reduction by Esso, the price of the more popular 95-octane petrol at major fuel companies now ranges from $3.56 at SPC to $3.60 at Caltex, Esso, Shell and Sinopec.

Meanwhile, Union Gas-owned Cnergy and Smart Energy are offering the petrol grade at $2.74 and $2.62 respectively.

Meanwhile, US West Texas Intermediate futures for December climbed $1.29 or 1.6 per cent to US$84.55.

The December contract expires on Friday.

During a trilateral meeting between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese and Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, Trump said he and Xi felt strongly about oil having to flow through the Strait of Hormuz.

Still, risks remained for Middle East oil supply amid renewed hostilities in the region.

On Nov 18, Iran said it targeted US drone and missile sites in Kuwait overnight after the United States struck Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, marking Tehran's first attack on the US-allied Gulf state since September.

The next day, on Nov 19, Riyadh's tallest skyscraper, headquarters of the Saudi sovereign wealth fund, was struck by a suspected Houthi missile in the latest blow in the Iran-backed Yemeni group's war with the kingdom.

data.title: Stocks fall as Anthropic debut fails to ease AI concerns; dollar rises
data.description:
NEW YORK/LONDON — Global stocks fell on Thursday (Nov 19) with sliding tech shares as Anthropic's debut failed to allay investor concerns about AI returns, while oil prices rose as attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz grabbed market attention.

Investors have said that Anthropic's market reception over the coming days and weeks will be heavily scrutinized to gauge broader sentiment toward investments in artificial intelligence. The Claude developer's initial public offering was priced at US$83 (S$107) a share, valuing Anthropic at about US$1.5 trillion before the stock rose as much as 39 per cent to trade at US$115.10.

"Investors are making changes in their portfolio to incorporate Anthropic, so I wouldn't extrapolate a whole lot of meaning from (Thursday's) trading behaviour, whether it's up or down," said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital in St. Louis.

Ellerbroek pointed to a leadership change in chipmaker Nvidia and to shrinking bets on the growth in data centre capex as having an impact on investors.

"Data centres are going to be more expensive to build and they're going to be built more slowly," Ellerbroek said.

Anthropic's stock closed up 17 per cent on its debut, valuing the company at just below US$1.8 trillion.

"We can't underestimate the importance of this IPO. It sort of serves as a valuation for the wider AI ecosystem," said Fiona Cincotta, senior market analyst at StoneX.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1,101.11 points, or 2.19 per cent, to 49,097.06, the S&P 500 fell 147.80 points, or 2.02 per cent, to 7,175.83 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 550.68 points, or 2.25 per cent, to 23,879.20.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe fell 17.76 points, or 1.65 per cent, to 1,056.80. The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 0.88 per cent, while emerging market stocks fell 18.79 points, or 1.27 per cent, to 1,465.49.

 Dollar and oil edge higher

The dollar ticked up against developed peers but some sensitive currencies sold off on concerns about tightening financial conditions. Mexico's peso fell 1.4 per cent and Colombia's peso dropped 1.8 per cent.

"We're seeing a scramble for US dollar liquidity, and the entire emerging market complex is suffering a severe selloff as global financial conditions tighten," said Karl Schamotta, chief market strategist at Corpay.

"With sentiment on the US technology sector showing signs of crumbling while expectations for the Fed's policy path climb, stress is rising in the currencies most exposed to a slowdown in the AI buildout," Schamotta said.

Against a basket of peers, the greenback has climbed to 19-month highs on the back of expectations of tighter monetary policy out of Washington. On Thursday, the dollar index rose for an eighth consecutive session and was up 0.14 per cent to 103.96.

In commodities, oil prices settled flat on the day but were higher late as earlier reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz more than offset rising US crude inventories and forecasts for a global oil surplus.

Iran's navy said in a statement carried by state media that two oil tankers hit naval mines in the waterway and "exploded" on Thursday. Reuters could not independently verify the report.

US crude rose 0.66 per cent to US$83.81 a barrel and Brent rose to US$92.72 per barrel, up 0.84 per cent on the day.

Spot gold fell 2.54 per cent to US$3,627.55 an ounce, and spot silver fell 4.36 per cent to US$43.04 an ounce. Copper declined 0.14 per cent to US$12,453.00 a ton.

Source: Reuters

data.title: Oil settles flat as Hormuz disruptions offset global surplus fears
data.description:
NEW YORK - Oil prices settled little changed on Thursday (Nov 19), as reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz offset pressure from rising US crude inventories and forecasts for a global oil surplus.

Brent crude futures settled up 3 cents, or 0.03 per cent, at US$91.98 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate crude eased 5 cents, or 0.06 per cent, to settle at US$83.21 a barrel, the lowest since August 26.

Two oil tankers hit naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday and "exploded," Iran's navy said in a statement carried by state media. Reuters could not independently verify the report.

The Iran-aligned Houthi movement also fired missiles at the Saudi Arabian capital Riyadh.

Saudi Arabia's civil defence said on Thursday that the attack damaged several floors of Riyadh's tallest skyscraper, headquarters of the Saudi sovereign wealth fund, and nearby buildings, but no injuries were reported, state news agency SPA reported. 

Earlier, two Western officials briefed by the Saudis said the kingdom is preparing for war against Yemen's Houthis to stretch well into next year.

"Rising Iranian attacks are weighing on Middle Eastern exports just as China ramps up crude imports, reducing oil on water and tightening the oil market," said UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo.

Cumulative losses from the Middle East conflict have now reached 2.8 billion barrels of oil and 60 billion cubic metres of gas supply from the Gulf, the International Energy Agency said on Thursday.

The IEA, however, added that the conflict could cut world oil demand by more than 4 per cent by 2035 if governments accelerate electrification, efficiency and fuel-switching measures in response.

Russia's crude oil output could fall again as Ukrainian attacks on refineries and export infrastructure intensify. Reuters, citing industry sources, reported on Wednesday that Ukrainian drone attacks have reduced Russian oil refineries' combined crude processing volumes by 45 per cent since late October.

Separately on Thursday, Russian President Vladimir Putin said that Moscow would hit back hard after Ukraine struck the bridge linking Russia and Crimea for a third time this week and said he was dropping any idea of a moratorium on attacking energy sectors and shipping.

Surplus supply

Despite geopolitical risks, signs of ample supply and a meeting between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese and Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Putin, weighed on the market.

The three leaders agreed on a symbolic "peace declaration" at an unprecedented three-way meeting on Thursday and reaffirmed that nuclear war should never be fought and pledged to increase fuel products for all countries.

Trump said both he and Xi felt strongly about oil having to flow through the Strait of Hormuz, and separately said the US would "see what happens" in its conflict with Iran after January 1, without explaining what the significance of that date might be.

Republicans in the US Senate rejected legislation directing Trump to end the war in Iran or obtain Congress' approval to continue it.

Elsewhere, a report from the Joint Organisations Data Initiative reinforced concerns of a supply glut after it reported that Saudi Arabia's crude exports rose nearly 21 per cent in September from August to 5.38 million barrels per day, the highest level since February.

On Wednesday, the Energy Information Administration reported a larger-than-expected build in US oil inventories.

Adding to expectations of surpluses, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Washington was considering ramping up diesel and oil exports to Europe, where the US has become the leading supplier since the US-Iran war began.

"Crude oil is caught between growing supplies and the continuing threat of war-related disruptions. Markets crave stability, and right now, they're finding very little of it," Tim Snyder, chief economist at Matador Economics, said.

Source: Reuters

data.title: Asian gasoline margin plunges to over 3-year lows on ample supplies
data.description:
NEW DELHI - Asian gasoline margins plummeted around 69 per cent this week as abundant supplies from China and the Middle East weighed on crack spreads, traders and analysts said on Thursday (Nov 19).

The refining profit, or crack, for gasoline shrank to US$2.67 per barrel over Brent crude, the lowest level since October 2023, from a record peak of US$50.53 on Oct 1.

"Increased Chinese exports are further weighing on the sentiment," Stuti Jhunjhunwala, oil market analyst at Energy Aspects, said.

Gasoline crack spreads usually shrink heading into the northern hemisphere's winter, when fuel demand falls, however, this year they hit record highs on a tight supply outlook, caused by the Middle East war, Russia's export ban and lower inventories at key trading hubs.

The margins fell to six-month lows at the end of October and have been on a downward trend since amid hopes of higher supplies.

"Plenty of supplies from China and year-end destocking causing the fall," a Dubai-based light distillate trader said.

Meanwhile, gasoline imports at the Singapore trading and blending hub tanked 69 per cent to 67,000 tons (about 566,000 barrels) in the week to Nov 18, while exports rose about 13 per cent on-week to roughly 459,000 tons, government data showed.

The top supplier was China at about 50,000 tons, while the top destination for exports was Australia at 111,000 tons.

Source: Reuters

data.title: GTA VI to supercharge Sony — but not so much in Japan
data.description:
TOKYO — The global launch of Grand Theft Auto VI on Thursday (Nov 18) is expected to provide a major boost to PlayStation maker Sony, though in its home market of Japan, the franchise remains a niche pursuit.

The long-awaited open-world crime action game from Take-Two Interactive's Rockstar Games is rolling out across the world and has been met with rave reviews and fans taking time off work to play.

About three-quarters of the 17 million GTA VI units sold are on PlayStation, according to estimates from Sensor Tower, outselling Xbox maker Microsoft.

Shares in Sony, whose PlayStation 5 console is in its seventh year on the market, were up almost three per cent in Tokyo compared with flat trading in the benchmark index.

Analysts think the global enthusiasm is unlikely to reach a fever pitch in Japan, where Switch 2 maker Nintendo dominates the gaming device market and consumers prefer anime-style titles to realistic, violent Western games.

"The current trends in Japan don't really fit this kind of game," said Toyo Securities analyst Hideki Yasuda.

Given worldwide demand, "there's absolutely no need for this game to sell in Japan", he said.

Earlier this year Sony scored a major global success with movie Spider-Man: Brand New Day but in Japan faced competition from breakout hit Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of Mermaid Island.

"A few of my friends bought GTA VI at midnight but I'm in no hurry to as it's only on PS5 and Xbox and you can't play multiplayer online yet," said Sorataka Goto, 33, who was shopping in Tokyo's Akihabara electronics district.

"If and when it's on PC and you can play online I'll consider buying it," said Goto, who bought the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

Nintendo has sold more than five million copies of the Switch 2 title, which was originally on the Nintendo 64, in the first four days since its launch earlier this month.

"I had the original as a child and so was excited to try this version," he said.

Japan not immune to GTA VI hype

Gamers in Japan may struggle to fully understand the satirical elements of GTA VI, the references to the Florida lifestyle and Western memes, said Serkan Toto, founder of game industry consultancy Kantan Games.

Still, the worldwide hype for GTA VI is spilling over to Japan and marketing in the country is unprecedented for a Western-made game, he said.

In Akihabara, a large poster featuring the lead characters, Lucia Caminos ​and Jason Duval, was plastered on the side of a building.

"'GTA VI' will not become a mega blockbuster in Japan but it will do very, very well," Toto said.

Analysts expect the release of "GTA VI" to soften the decline of PS5 hardware sales this year and support growth in software sales.

Sony sold 2.6 million PS5 units during the July to September quarter, which analysts see as reflecting demand ahead of GTA VI, down from four million a year earlier.

"We've modelled PlayStation profits materially ahead of the Street in the next couple of quarters, on account of the GTA VI launch," Bernstein analyst David Dai wrote in a note.

The release is bolstering Sony's games slate after it delayed the launch of God of War Laufey by three months to May 2027.

Sony is grappling with procurement challenges as the cost of memory chips has risen sharply due to the AI boom.

"I don't get the sense that Sony has much desire to aggressively sell hardware... the benefits Sony gets from royalties will be enormous," said Toyo Securities' Yasuda.

data.title: Dollar eases after seven-session rally, rates and equities in focus
data.description:
The US dollar index edged down on Thursday (Nov 19) after a seven-session winning streak but remained underpinned by hawkish remarks from a Federal Reserve official that reinforced the case for further rate hikes.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller called for a more aggressive response to inflation, while minutes of the central bank's Oct 27 to 28 meeting showed policymakers increasingly concerned that additional tightening might be needed.

The dollar rally started on Nov 10 when hotter-than-expected US inflation data bolstered expectations that the Fed would raise borrowing costs next month.

The dollar index this week reached its highest level since April 2, 2025, when US President Donald Trump revealed a sweeping tariff package, triggering a selloff in US assets.

It was last down 0.05 per cent at 103.73, after reaching 103.97.

Barclays analysts said fiscal stimulus and strong AI-related capital spending point to a resilient US economy, a wider output gap and higher-for-longer interest rates, all supportive of dollar strength.

The dollar's gains have come despite a selloff in technology shares.

"First, the market has also repriced a more hawkish Fed given recent commentary pushing the interest rate differential wider, but the dollar seems to be overshooting this move," said George Saravelos, global head of forex strategy at Deutsche Bank, explaining the recent rise.

"Second, and more intriguingly, foreigners have been very aggressive buyers of US equities even as the stock market has tumbled," he added.

A Deutsche Bank tracker following more than 100 foreign-domiciled exchange-traded funds showed large dip-buying of US stocks by foreigners over the last two weeks, the biggest buying spree so far this year.

Such a move reinforces the view that the dollar has been supported by investor flows into US equities.

Shares in Nvidia fell overnight even after the chip bellwether beat revenue and guidance forecasts, amid uncertainty caused by co-founder Jensen Huang's sudden departure as CEO last week following his admission of extramarital affairs.

Safe-haven flows boost the yen

The dollar was up 0.25 per cent to 159.75 yen, snapping a four-day losing streak.

Analysts said that a further selloff in AI-linked assets could support the yen through safe-haven buying and repatriation flows, with the impact likely to be more pronounced against other currencies than against the dollar.

According to Barclays estimates, a 10 per cent decline in the S&P 500 from its peak could push dollar/yen towards 155, while a 20 per cent decline could pressure it towards 152.

The euro was up 0.34 per cent versus the Japanese currency at 175.43, after falling about 1.5 per cent since late last week.

The Aussie dropped as low as $0.6662 for the first time since January. Australia's employment fell for a second straight month in October and the jobless rate climbed to a five-year high, bolstering the view that rates have likely peaked.

Following the data, UBS economist George Tharenou brought forward his forecast for the first Reserve Bank of Australia rate cut to August next year from November, and extended the easing cycle to three cuts from two, citing elevated inflation and a deterioration in the labour and housing markets.

Source: Reuters

data.title: Toyota to recall over 314,000 US vehicles over Takata air bag rupture risk, NHTSA says
data.description:
Toyota Motor is recalling 314,029 vehicles in the US because front passenger air bag inflators made by Takata may rupture and hurl metal fragments at occupants, the US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Thursday (Nov 19).

The recall covers vehicles from model years 2002 to 2017, including the Lexus SC430, IS250 and GX460, and the Toyota Corolla, Tundra, Sequoia and 4Runner.

Toyota said it has received no reports of ruptures involving the affected inflators, according to the NHTSA recall report.

The automaker said the inflators were nearing the end of their estimated safe service life and could rupture if a front passenger air bag deploys.

Toyota said it is conducting the recall out of an abundance of caution, according to NHTSA.

NHTSA said certain Takata front passenger air bag inflators in these vehicles could rupture due to propellant degradation after long-term exposure to high humidity, high temperatures and high temperature cycling.

Depending on the vehicle, dealers will replace the front passenger air bag inflator or the air bag assembly free of charge, the agency said.

Source: Reuters

data.title: Amazon targets as many as 30,000 corporate job cuts, sources say
data.description:
SAN FRANCISCO - Amazon is planning to cut as many as 30,000 corporate jobs beginning on Tuesday (Oct 28), as the company pares expenses and compensates for overhiring during the peak demand of the pandemic, according to three people familiar with the matter.

The figure represents a small percentage of Amazon's 1.55 million total employees, but nearly 10 per cent of its roughly 350,000 corporate employees. This would mark Amazon's largest job cut since late 2022, when it started to eliminate around 27,000 positions.

An Amazon spokesperson declined to comment.

Amazon has been trimming smaller numbers of jobs over the past two years across multiple divisions, including devices, communications and podcasting. The cuts beginning this week may affect a variety of divisions, including human resources, known as People Experience and Technology or PXT; operations, devices and services; and Amazon Web Services, the people said.

Managers of impacted teams were asked to undergo training on Monday for how to communicate with staff following email notifications that will start going out on Tuesday morning, the people said.

Amazon CEO Andy Jassy is undertaking an initiative to reduce what he has described as an excess of bureaucracy, including by reducing the number of managers. He installed an anonymous complaint line for identifying inefficiencies that has elicited some 1,500 responses and over 450 process changes, he said earlier this year.

Jassy said in June that the increased use of artificial intelligence tools would likely lead to further job cuts, particularly through automating repetitive and routine tasks.

"This latest move signals that Amazon is likely realising enough AI-driven productivity gains within corporate teams to support a substantial reduction in force," said Sky Canaves, an eMarketer analyst. "Amazon has also been under pressure in the short-term to offset the long-term investments in building out its AI infrastructure."

The full scope of this round of job cuts was not immediately clear. The people familiar with the matter said the number could change over time as Amazon's financial priorities shift. Fortune earlier reported that the human resources division could be targeted with a cut of roughly 15 per cent.

A programme begun early this year to bring employees back in the office five days per week, among tech's most stringent, has failed to generate sufficient attrition, said two of the people, citing that as another reason for the size of the layoff. Some of the employees who are not swiping in daily because they live far from corporate offices, or for other reasons, are being told they have voluntarily quit Amazon and must leave without severance, a savings for the company.

Layoffs.fyi, a website tracking tech job cuts, estimated that about 98,000 jobs have been lost so far this year among 216 companies. For all of 2024, the figure was 153,000.

Amazon's largest profit centre, cloud computing unit AWS, reported second-quarter sales of $30.9 billion (S$40 billion), a 17.5 per cent increase that was well below gains of 39 per cent for Microsoft's Azure and of 32 per cent for Alphabet's Google Cloud.

Estimates indicate that AWS will have boosted third-quarter sales by about 18 per cent to $32 billion, a slight slowdown from last year's 19 per cent increase. AWS is still reeling from a roughly 15-hour internet outage last week that felled many of the most popular online services, like Snapchat and Venmo.

Amazon appears to be expecting another big holiday selling season. It plans to offer 250,000 seasonal jobs to help staff warehouses, among other needs, the same as in the prior two years.

Amazon on Friday also announced a reorganisation of a segment of its PXT unit focused on diversity initiatives, a memo reviewed by Reuters showed. The changes largely involved promoting people to new roles.

Amazon shares rose 1.2 per cent to $226.97 on Monday. The company plans to report third-quarter earnings on Thursday.

data.title: When 'fringe' homes cross $2,000 psf, has Singapore's idea of 'prime' changed for good?
data.description:
You know a big change is coming, when longstanding classifications and definitions come to a close.

For example, back in 2024, when HDB decided to abandon the "mature" versus "non-mature" classification for flats. A move that makes sense because for years now, "developed" has been a concept that's much more localised; something you'd understand if you live right next to a mall and an MRT station, but your neighbourhood keeps getting called "ulu."

So the change in the classification system reflected changes on the ground; and as we enter 2025, I feel the same thing might be happening to another old concept: regions. By this, I mean the Core Central Region (CCR), Rest of Central Region (RCR), and Outside of Central Region (OCR).

Now I'm not so bold as to assert these mean nothing — for now, they definitely carry weight. But there are some creeping changes that hint that, at some point in the future, the notion of OCR, RCR, and CCR may be as obsolete as "mature versus non-mature."

Observable behaviour is a good place to start. I know this is anecdotal, but it's hard to ignore: ask around and see how many Singaporeans still "go to town" (by which I mean an area like Orchard) for their weekend retail therapy, or just to hang out. I suspect that, more often these days, you hear names like Tampines Mall, Waterway Point, NEX, etc., rather than ION Orchard or Ngee Ann City.

I've met Singaporeans who haven't "gone to town" for so long, their eyes glaze over when I mention Orchard Central or Wheelock; and they need to think really hard to remember what would make them travel all the way there.

These days, most people have everything they need within a short bus ride or walk from their front door. Whether it's groceries, restaurants, clinics, or entertainment, chances are it's a few blocks from you, or about two to three stops by bus. Maybe back in the '90s or before, the nearby amenities were just minimarts and hair salons. But today? I'm willing to bet a huge number of you reading this, right now, could get to a Din Tai Fung, Starbucks, Lululemon, Uniqlo, etc., in 15 minutes or under.

And this is not even the end-point of our decentralisation: it's still a work in progress, so it will be more pronounced in future. When you consider all the separate hubs and nodes, is the OCR really "fringe" anymore?

Then there's the way prices have changed

Earlier this year, the median PSF for OCR condos clocked in at $2,554 psf. This was a mere sliver away from the RCR, which registered S$2,386 psf (you can find a little more detail on that here.) CCR condos, meanwhile, are at around $2,800 to $3,300 psf — this happens to be below the 2024 CCR average of $3,305 psf.

Meanwhile, in the OCR, we see condos like Springleaf Residence reach around $2,064 psf, while Canberra Crescent Residences went for around $1,974 psf. Now, of course, I'm aware that the actual total price (the quantum) is lower as the units are built to be affordable; but it doesn't change the fact that these are numbers we'd never have associated with the "most affordable" region in the previous decade.

More to the point, we're seeing CCR prices flattening, while RCR and especially OCR prices rise. Now, combine that with the reality on the ground: residents in most parts of the OCR no longer have significantly worse amenities compared to those in the RCR or CCR. In fact, some parts of the CCR are even arguably worse off, like Marina Bay with its lack of school access.

This shift is further supported by an ageing population.

Older residents are less inclined to travel far for errands, meals, or entertainment. I'm not even 50, and already I dread the thought of taking the train all the way to Bugis for late-night hot pot. And more to the point, why would I when there's probably a Haidilao closer to me.

*Note: I just Googled it and yes, there's one two bus stops away. I'm in a very new neighbourhood, and I could still predict that even before I had to Google it.

And to their credit, URA's push to decentralise anticipated this very trend. The convenience of having a clinic, supermarket, and food court nearby isn't just a lifestyle perk — someone in charge knew it would be a necessity for an ageing society.

It's just a happy coincidence that it would also make access to amenities more equal; and in that process, gradually erode the price difference by region.

So where do we go from here? I think we'll have a new way to define things — but in future, we'll probably be assessing and pricing convenience by how far things are from their given neighbourhood hub; and less so by which general district or region they're in.

It's worth thinking about, if you end up weighing your choices between an RCR or CCR condo, or an OCR and RCR condo. That technical distinction may matter less a long time from now, at the point of resale — so maybe focus on ground-level things like which one is a shorter walk to the nearest mall.
